title: July Monarchy
capsule: The July Monarchy (Monarchie de Juillet) was the constitutional regime of France from August 1830 to February 1848, established after the July Revolution drove out Charles X and installed Louis-Philippe of the Orléans branch on the throne. Louis-Philippe governed as a 'citizen-king,' ruling under a liberalized charter and forging close ties with the haute bourgeoisie; François Guizot dominated the ministry from 1840. France expanded its colonial presence dramatically in this period, consolidating the conquest of Algeria begun in 1830 and opening commercial engagements in West Africa and Southeast Asia. The regime collapsed in the Revolution of February 1848, when street barricades in Paris and the defection of the National Guard forced Louis-Philippe to abdicate, leading to the proclamation of the Second French Republic.
